'''Jorge André Swieca''' was a [[:Category:Brazilian physicists|Brazilian physicist]] born in [[Warsaw]], [[Poland]] in 1936.<ref name=EPJH>
{{cite journal
 |author=B. Schroer
 |year=2010
 |title=Jorge A. Swieca's contributions to quantum field theory in the 60s and 70s and their relevance in present research
 |journal=[[European Physical Journal H]]
 |volume=35 |issue=1 |pages=53–88
 |doi=10.1140/epjh/e2010-00004-1
 |arxiv=0712.0371
|bibcode = 2010EPJH...35...53S |s2cid=119287964
 }}</ref> He was mostly active in [[quantum field theory]] (QFT), particularly during the 1960s and 1970s.<ref name=EPJH/> A series of summer schools is named after him.<ref>
{{cite book
 |editor1=G.A. Alves |editor2=O.J.P. Éboli |editor3=V.O. Rivelles |year=2002
 |title=Proceedings of the XI Jorge André Swieca Summer School: Particles and Fields
 |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=tqpN0B9X6bcC&q=Jorge+A.+Swieca
 |publisher=[[World Scientific]]
 |isbn=981-238-021-3
}}</ref>

Swieca fled Poland with his parent during [[World War II]], shortly after it was occupied by [[Russia]] and [[Germany]].<ref name=EPJH/> They spent two years in [[Japan]], before moving to [[Rio de Janeiro]], [[Brazil]].<ref name=EPJH/> He obtained his PhD from the [[University of São Paulo]] under Werner Güttinger in 1964.<ref name=EPJH/> He died in December 1980, after complications from a [[heart bypass surgery]].<ref name=EPJH/><ref>
{{cite journal
 |author1=B. Schroer |author2=A.L.L. Videira |year=1981
 |title=Jorge Andre Swieca |journal=[[Physics Today]]
 |volume=34 |issue=5 |pages=97
 |doi=10.1063/1.2914592
 |doi-access=
 |bibcode = 1981PhT....34e..97S }}</ref> In the late 1960s, he received the Brazilian Santista science prize.<ref name=EPJH/>
